name: clean-code
description: Robert C. Martin's Clean Code as eleven routing knowledge-base skills: one per language with a solid community adaptation, plus a shared core for everything else. Each is a chaptered reference — rules, worked examples, a cheatsheet, a glossary and a pattern catalogue — and each description routes to the right sibling, so the model loads the one skill that fits the file it is editing; a SessionStart gateway names the dispatch. clean-code-java carries the original book (Java examples, the refactoring case studies, and the 66-item smells-and-heuristics catalogue). Nine skills carry the community adaptations, each worked in its own idiom: clean-code-typescript (TS types, Failable results), clean-code-javascript (closures, promises), clean-code-python (ABCs, dataclasses, mypy), clean-code-php (strict comparison, final classes behind interfaces), clean-code-csharp (properties, records, LINQ, async), clean-code-go (errors as values, small interfaces, scope and mutability), clean-code-ruby (duck typing, keyword arguments, blocks), clean-code-dart (named required parameters, cascades, null safety) and clean-code-swift (protocols, optionals, value types). clean-code-universal is the family's shared core: a language-agnostic distillation built on a three-tier spine that separates rules holding wherever you can name a thing and run a check (Tier 1) from rules binding only where a construct exists — a parameter list, a type system, an exception, a test runner, a thread (Tier 2). It carries the languages without a sibling — Rust, C++, C, Kotlin, Scala — and the declarative ones: YAML (Kubernetes, Helm, CI pipelines), Terraform/HCL, SQL, Bash, Dockerfile, with a translation table stating, per rule, what it means where there are no functions, no classes and no unit tests. Sources and licences differ per skill: see NOTICE.md.
